newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia army denies 300 died in Kalimantan riot.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia army denies 300 died in Kalimantan riot.

text.p: Indonesian armed forces commander General Feisal Tanjung has denied reports that around 300 people were killed in recent ethnic violence in West Kalimantan, newspapers reported on Friday.
"It is not true the number of people killed is 300. We will make an official announcement later," Tanjung was quoted as saying on Thursday by the Media Indonesia newspaper.

Tanjung, who gave no further details, said the military was still collecting information on the fatalities in the riot which rocked the province on the Indonesian side of Borneo island from late December to February.
Assistant to the army chief of staff for security affairs, Major-General Zacky Anwar Makarim, was quoted as saying on Monday by Media Indonesia that about 300 people had been killed in the unrest.
Makarim was denying a news report that the fatalities were as high as 2,000.
Military officials and residents in the province had previously said at least 12 people had died over the past six weeks.

Trouble erupted in West Kalimantan in late December in Sanggau Ledo, about 95 km (60 miles) north of the provincial capital Pontianak, between the native Dayaks and migrants from Madura island, which lies off the main island of Java, apparently after a fight over a girl.
Clashes lasted until early February and the military deployed about 3,000 troops in the province to contain unrest.

The Jakarta Post quoted Tanjung as saying the conflict was officially over since leaders of the warring parties signed a peace treaty on Tuesday. Most Dayaks are Christians while the Maduran migrants are Moslems.

However, the paper also quoted residents as saying there had been clashes in the Sungai Kunyit district, 56 km (34 miles) north of Pontianak, as recently as Tuesday with an unknown number of casualities and material losses.
